problem: Jacob has two email accounts, account $A$ and account $B.$ In account $A$ he receives $40%$ of his emails and he receives the remaining $60%$ in account $B.$ Approximately $30%$ of the emails received in account $A$ are spam and $36%$ of the emails received in both accounts are spam. What is the probability that a randomly selected email from account $B$ is spam? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

feedback.problem: A math teacher splits her calculus class into two groups, Group $A$ and Group $B.$ Of the total students, $35%$ of her students are in Group $A,$ and $65%$ are in Group $B.$ If $20%$ of the students in Group $A$ obtained the top grade, and the probability that a randomly selected student from either group obtained the top grade is $0.265,$ what is the probability that a randomly selected student from Group $B$ obtained the top grade? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $G$ be the event that the chosen student obtained the top grade, and let $A$ be the event that the student is from Group $A.$ Then ${A}^{′}$ is the event that the student is from Group $B.$

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected student obtained the top grade, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
P(G)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|{A}^{′})P({A}^{′})
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each bit of information into mathematical notation.

- Since $35%$ of her students are in Group $A$ and $65%$ are in Group $B,$ we have

$$
P(A)=0.35,\,P({A}^{′})=0.65.
$$

- Since $20%$ of the students in Group $A$ obtained the top grade, we have

$$
P(G|A)=0.20.
$$

- Since the probability that a randomly selected student from either group obtained the top  grade is $0.265,$ we have

$$
P(G)=0.265.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(G|{A}^{′}),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|{A}^{′})P({A}^{′}) \\ 0.265 & =(0.20)(0.35)+P(G|{A}^{′})(0.65) \\ 0.265 & =0.07+0.65P(G|{A}^{′}) \\ 0.65P(G|{A}^{′}) & =0.195 \\ P(G|{A}^{′}) & =0.30\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected student from Group $B$ obtained the top grade is $0.30.$
